signals.raise: USD 1bn minority stake sale at USD 8.65bn valuation (Dec 2025; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraken_Technologies)

name: Kraken Technologies
desc: Builds the Kraken operating platform that energy and water utilities use to run billing, customer service and smart-grid flexibility.
ownership: private: majority-owned by Octopus Energy Group
capacity_detail: Minority stake sold for USD 1bn in December 2025, valuing Kraken at USD 8.65bn
markets: Licensed by about 40 utilities in 27 countries, including UK, US, Europe, Australia and Japan; over 70 million accounts contracted
rationale: Planned demerger from Octopus makes a standalone global B2B brand; F1 hospitality reaches utility executives across its 27-country client base.

name: Topsoe
desc: Danish supplier of catalysts, process technology and solid oxide electrolysers for clean fuels, ammonia and hydrogen.
markets: Customers worldwide in refining, chemicals, aviation, marine, metals, cement and power; offices across Americas, Europe, Middle East and Asia
rationale: Positions as decarbonisation technology leader for aviation and heavy industry; F1's sustainable-fuel push from 2026 gives a direct technical story.

name: Enercon
desc: German manufacturer of gearless onshore wind turbines, installed in more than 50 countries, owned by the Aloys Wobben Foundation.
markets: Sales offices in 25 countries; turbines installed in more than 50 countries; production in Germany, Poland, Portugal and Turkey
rationale: Competes with listed rivals Vestas and Siemens Gamesa for European and emerging-market orders; F1 offers B2B hospitality and an engineering-precision narrative.

name: Fronius International
desc: Austrian maker of solar inverters, welding systems and battery-charging technology with 36 subsidiaries worldwide.
markets: 36 international subsidiaries and sales partners in more than 60 countries across Europe, Americas, Asia and Australia
rationale: Inverter brand selling to installers and homeowners against SMA and Huawei; welding and charging lines also suit motorsport engineering storytelling.

name: St1
desc: Nordic fuel retailer and refiner producing renewable HVO diesel, waste-based ethanol and liquefied biogas for transport.
markets: Fuel stations and energy operations in Finland, Sweden, Norway and the United Kingdom
rationale: Consumer-facing fuel brand pushing renewable fuels; F1's 100% sustainable fuel era gives a credible link for Nordic and UK forecourt marketing.

name: Vaillant Group
desc: Family-owned German maker of heat pumps, boilers and cooling systems sold in more than 60 countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue about EUR 3.3bn (Wikipedia infobox as of June 2026)
markets: Brands present in more than 60 countries; production in five European countries, Turkey and China
rationale: Heat-pump growth depends on consumer brand trust in Europe; F1's large German and UK audiences suit a household-name decarbonisation message.

sponsorships: Jersey sponsor TBV Lemgo handball; Swiss Cup football sponsor (2010)
name: Stiebel Eltron
desc: German family-owned manufacturer of heat pumps, ventilation and hot-water appliances with subsidiaries in Europe, Asia and the US.
ownership: family-owned: Stiebel family foundation and Frank Stiebel
markets: Subsidiaries in ten European countries, China, Japan, Thailand and the United States; sales representatives in 20 countries
rationale: Already uses sports sponsorship for brand building; heat-pump makers need consumer awareness in Germany and UK, both core F1 markets.
